title: Automated reconciliation and corrective transfers for misattributed tenant usage (tenant-alias scenarios)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem summary: During tenant migrations, aliasing, and reserved-pool reassignments we observe short-lived misattributed token usage where requests are recorded against the 'old' tenant ID while billing and quota enforcement are expected against the 'new' tenant ID. This causes incorrect quota exhaustion, customer-facing rate-limits being applied to the wrong account, and downstream billing mismatches. Root causes identified so far: 1) delayed sync between auth service and quota ledger on tenant alias update; 2) edge routing sending a small fraction of traffic to legacy tenant contexts during rolling upgrades; 3) race conditions in reserved pool handover where leases are reacquired under the previous owner for a few seconds.

Scope: Build an automated reconciler and corrective transfer mechanism that: (a) detects misattributed usage windows for reserved pools and tenant aliases across daily/rolling windows; (b) computes safe corrective ledger adjustments (token-level transfers) and updates quota state so the new tenant sees the correct remaining quota; (c) provides a dry-run audit trail, admin approval flow, and automatic retries for idempotency; (d) integrates with billing reporting so invoices reflect corrections; (e) surfaces clear telemetry and customer-impact flags.
background_and_motivation: We already have manual scripts and a small runbook used by SRE/Revenue Ops for high-severity cases. Manual work is slow and error-prone for low-volume but high-frequency alias events. As we grow Dedicated and Private deployments, handovers will become more common and manual remediation will not scale. Automating detection + safe correction will reduce both customer-support load and invoicing noise while preventing inadvertent user-facing rate limits.
proposal: Design a two-phase system: (1) Detection engine that runs hourly and marks candidate misattribution windows. Detection heuristics include overlapping API-key/session fingerprints, near-identical request IPs/ASN clusters, identical user-agent + short timestamp drift, and reserved-pool lease overlap markers. Each candidate is scored for confidence and potential customer impact. (2) Correction pipeline that only runs for high-confidence candidates and performs: a) ledger transfer transaction (delta tokens moved from old tenant ledger to new tenant ledger) guarded by multi-stage validation (signature, checksum of pre-transfer counters); b) quota state replay for affected tenants to recompute remaining burst/bucket values; c) generation of an audit event and optional notification to customer success and the tenant's billing contact. All operations must be atomic w.r.t. invoice snapshot and produce compensating actions if any step fails. We will initially gate the pipeline behind a feature flag with a dry-run mode and center it on reserved-capacity customers (higher impact).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Detection engine finds seeded misattribution cases in the dedicated test harness with >98% precision and >92% recall. 2) Correction pipeline (dry-run) produces a reconciled ledger and an audit log for seeded scenarios without changing live quotas. 3) End-to-end integration test: apply corrective transfer to a synthetic reserved pool tenant pair and verify quota enforcement moves to expected tenant and billing export shows corrected lines. 4) No regressions on performance of quota evaluation service (latency P50/P95 within 5% of baseline during reconciliation runs). 5) Operations can run a manual review UI to approve/reject corrections before any money-affecting ledger changes.
design_considerations:
- Idempotency: every transfer must be keyed by (detection_run_id, candidate_hash) and be safe to retry.
- Atomicity: use a two-phase commit between ledger store and quota controller, or leverage a single DB transaction where possible.
- Safety thresholds: only auto-correct when candidate_score >= 0.85 OR when the transfer amount is below a customer-tier-specific min threshold. Above threshold require manual approval.
- Observability: create a reconciliation dashboard (counts of candidates, transfers performed, failures, manual approvals) and a reconciliation audit index that surfaces before/after token balances.
- Privacy & compliance: corrections must follow audit retention policies and cannot expose raw request bodies in audit logs.
- Backwards compatibility: do not change existing quota evaluation APIs; corrections are applied via ledger adjustment and quota replay.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): detection engine prototype + test harness, seed with historical alias incidents. Phase 2 (3 sprints): correction pipeline dry-run implementation, audit logging, and QA on synthetic tenants. Phase 3 (1 sprint): admin UI for review and approval + feature-flag ramp to 10% of reserved customers. Phase 4 (rolling): full enablement for reserved customers and optional opt-in for hosted customers. Code owner: billing/usage-service team. Required infra changes: lightweight job runner, reconciliation index datastore (append-only), and orchestration to coordinate ledger+quota commits.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy detection-only to prod with no side effects; monitor false positives for 2 weeks. 2) Enable dry-run corrections for internal Ops and validate outputs against manual runbook for 1 week. 3) Open admin approval UI; allow Revenue Ops to accept small-dollar corrections (<= $50 equivalent) automatically. 4) Gradually increase auto-approve threshold and customer coverage over 4 weeks. 5) After 30 days of stable operation, remove dry-run gating for qualified reserved-pool customers.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental double-crediting or missing invoice lines. Mitigation: require a checksum reconciliation step and produce compensating transactions in case of divergence; all money-facing actions must go through Revenue Ops approval for the first month. Risk: detection false positives creating noise. Mitigation: conservative scoring and initial dry-run enforcement. Risk: latency impact to quota evaluation. Mitigation: run heavy reconciliation work off the critical path and use snapshot/read-replicas for ledger reads.
